titleEn: 'Dagongren': How Chinese Workers Turned Labor into a Rallying Cry
summaryEn: Dagongren, 'working person', is China's half-joking badge of wage labor — self-deprecating, unifying, and famous for 'Good morning, dagongren!'

symbolLayer.explanation: '打工'(体力劳动式务工)+'人'，把白领工作降格为体力劳动，形成自嘲
symbolLayer.explanationEn: 'Da gong' (manual-labor work) + 'ren' (person): white-collar work downgraded to manual labor, used for self-mockery.

origin: 2020年B站UP主'抽象带篮子'视频走红，引发全网打工人语录创作潮
originEn: A 2020 Bilibili creator's video went viral, sparking a wave of dagongren catchphrases.
usage: 上班族自嘲身份，用幽默消解职场压力，'早安，打工人'为标志性语录
usageEn: Office workers mocking their own identity to defuse workplace pressure; 'Good morning, dagongren!' is the signature line.
commonMisreading: 被当作纯粹抱怨或丧文化，实际是带幽默感的团结式自嘲，类似英语'we're all wage slaves'的战友情
commonMisreadingEn: Read as pure complaint or a 'giving-up' culture; it's actually humorous, uniting self-mockery — like the camaraderie of 'we're all wage slaves'.

memeLineage.event: B站视频'打工人'语录走红
全网'早安打工人'语录与表情包复制潮
memeLineage.eventEn: 'Good morning, dagongren' quotes and stickers flood the internet

memeLineage.eventEn: 'Wei kuan ren' and 'gan fan ren' among the 'XX-ren' variants

memeLineage.eventEn: Reddit r/antiwork picks up the 'dagongren' concept

memeLineage.eventEn: Overseas media compare it with quiet quitting; the concept flows back to Chinese discourse
